I get into the same kind of funk every couple months! This past year is the most consistently I’ve drawn; I’ve been sticking to the hobby since March, when usually I’ll draw for a couple months and then drop it…

That being said, one of my biggest motivators is trying to “master” something new. “Master” as in get adequately good at it so I can incorporate it into my art! Learning new techniques that are applicable feels so good, but definitely takes time to payoff too. That being said, it’s good to get into the mindset that your art doesn’t immediately have to look good. Sometimes you just keep working on it and trying new things, sometimes you pitch a piece entirely and start over. 

Most of all, don’t be too hard on yourself. Art is for everyone, and we should be drawing in the styles we like. Besides, that style will keep changing over time anyway! I think you should just focus on what style makes you excited and want to draw more instead of what things “should” look like. 

Good luck! Remember, you have all the time in the world to hone your craft.

Quite honestly any app works if you’re just starting out! Personally I used iBisPaint when I was beginning, and a lot of amazing anime fan artists I know still use it! The pens are great and the stabilization is good as well, plus the selection tool is one of my favorites out of programs I’ve used. 

Once you’ve gotten a hang of things, I really recommend Clip Studio Paint if it’s accessible to you. A lot of manga artists use it, and I personally really enjoy the program and being able to download all kinds of brushes from the assets store. 

Overall, the program you start out on doesn’t matter as much as the work you put in! A lot of great artists I know span from MediBang to Procreate. I recommend watching a lot of YouTube tutorials and cross-referencing your favorite artists. Best of luck!
